arxiv-1712-07209.title: Flat affine subvarieties in Oeljeklaus-Toma manifolds
arxiv-1712-07209.creator: Liviu Ornea
arxiv-1712-07209.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Liviu Ornea. Abstract: The Oeljeklaus-Toma (OT-) manifolds are compact, complex, non-Kähler manifolds constructed by Oeljeklaus and Toma, and generalizing the Inoue surfaces. Their construction uses the number-theoretic data: a number field K and a torsion-free subgroup U in the group of units of the ring of integers of K , with rank of U equal to the number of real embeddings of K .

arxiv-2203-03225.title: Ultrafast optical observation of spin-pumping induced dynamic exchange coupling in ferromagnetic semiconductor/metal bilayer
arxiv-2203-03225.creator: X. Liu, P. Liu, H. C. Yuan, J. Y. Shi, H. L. Wang, S. H. Nie, F. Jin, Z. Zheng, X. Z. Yu, J. H. Zhao, H. B. Zhao, G. Lüpke
arxiv-2203-03225.description: Abstract Spin angular momentum transfer in magnetic bilayers offers the possibility of ultrafast and low-loss operation for next-generation spintronic devices. We report the field- and temperature- dependent measurements on the magnetization precessions in Co 2 FeAl/(Ga,Mn)As by time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TRMOKE).

arxiv-2302-02037.title: Bounds on Binary Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman LCD codes
arxiv-2302-02037.creator: Welington Santos
arxiv-2302-02037.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Welington Santos. Linear complementary dual codes (LCD codes) are codes whose intersections with their dual codes are trivial. These codes were introduced by Massey in 1992. LCD codes have wide applications in data storage, communication systems and cryptography. Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman LCD codes (NRT-LCD codes) were introduced by Heqian, Guangku and Wei as a generalization of LCD codes for the NRT metric space M n , s ​ ( 𝔽 q ) M_{n,s}(\mathbb{F}_{q}) .

arxiv-2406-03594.title: Why is “Problems” Predictive of Positive Sentiment? A Case Study of Explaining Unintuitive Features in Sentiment Classification
arxiv-2406-03594.creator: Jiaming Qu, Jaime Arguello, Yue Wang
arxiv-2406-03594.description: Abstract . Explainable AI (XAI) algorithms aim to help users understand how a machine learning model makes predictions. To this end, many approaches explain which input features are most predictive of a target label. However, such explanations can still be puzzling to users (e.g., in product reviews, the word “problems” is predictive of positive sentiment).

arxiv-2410-23845.title: The non-Hermitian skin effect: A perspective
arxiv-2410-23845.creator: Julius T. Gohsrich, Ayan Banerjee, Flore K. Kunst
arxiv-2410-23845.description: Abstract The non-Hermitian (NH) skin effect is a truly NH feature, which manifests itself as an accumulation of states, known as skin states, on the boundaries of a system. In this perspective, we discuss several aspects of the NH skin effect focusing on the most interesting facets of this phenomenon.

arxiv-2510-05358.title: On a class of almost Hermitian 4-manifolds
arxiv-2510-05358.creator: Ethan Addison, Tedi Drăghici, Mehdi Lejmi
arxiv-2510-05358.description: Abstract . Using an integral identity proved by Sekigawa [ 23 ] on compact almost Hermitian 4-manifolds, we naturally obtain a global characterization of the class 𝒜 ​ ℋ 1 \mathcal{AH}_{1} of almost Hermitian 4-manifolds satisfying the first Gray curvature condition from apparently weaker conditions.

arxiv-2511-05698.title: Probing Jet Compositions with Extreme Mass Ratio BinaryBlack Holes
arxiv-2511-05698.creator: Hung-Yi Pu
arxiv-2511-05698.description: Abstract Determining whether black hole jets are dominated by leptonic or baryonic matter remains an open question in high-energy astrophysics. We propose that extreme mass ratio binary (EMRB) black holes, where an intermediate mass secondary black hole (a “miniquasar”) periodically interacts with the accretion flow of a supermassive black hole (SMBH), offer a natural laboratory to probe jet composition.

pmc-10605538.title: E-Cadherin Is Expressed in Epithelial Cells of the Choroid Plexus in Human and Mouse Brains
pmc-10605538.creator: Genta Takebayashi, Yoichi Chiba, Keiji Wakamatsu, Ryuta Murakami, Yumi Miyai, Koichi Matsumoto, Naoya Uemura, Ken Yanase, Gotaro Shirakami, Yuichi Ogino, Masaki Ueno, Ilya Nikolaevich Medvedev, Svetlana Zavalishina, Vorobieva Nadezhda Viktorovna
pmc-10605538.description: Evidence showing the functional significance of the choroid plexus is accumulating. Epithelial cells with tight and adherens junctions of the choroid plexus play important roles in cerebrospinal fluid production and circadian rhythm formation. Although specific types of cadherin expressed in adherens junctions of choroid plexus epithelium (CPE) have been examined, they remained uncertain.

pmc-11389903.title: Police violence reduces trust in the police among Black residents
pmc-11389903.creator: Jonathan Ben-Menachem, Gerard Torrats-Espinosa
pmc-11389903.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent high-profile incidents involving the shooting or killing of unarmed Black men have intensified the debate about how police violence affects trust in the criminal justice system, particularly among communities of color. In this article, we propose a quasi-experimental design that leverages the timing of the shooting of Jacob Blake by the Kenosha Police Department relative to when a large survey was fielded in the city of Chicago.

pmc-11434991.title: Whole Plant Extracts for Neurocognitive Disorders: A Narrative Review of Neuropsychological and Preclinical Studies
pmc-11434991.creator: Alessandro Piva, Giulia Benvegnù, Stefano Negri, Mauro Commisso, Sofia Ceccato, Linda Avesani, Flavia Guzzo, Cristiano Chiamulera, Paola Coccetti, Paola Fusi
pmc-11434991.description: The incidence of neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer’s or Parkinson’s Disease, characterized by a progressive cognitive decline, is rising worldwide. Despite the considerable efforts to unveil the neuropsychological bases of these diseases, there is still an unmet medical need for effective therapies against cognitive deficits.

pmc-11456898.title: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma with obstructive pattern: A rare case of small bowel lymphoma
pmc-11456898.creator: Youssef Sleiman, Ribal Aby Hadeer, Hassan Nahle, Nawaf Jurdi, Leila Abs, Mustafa Allouch
pmc-11456898.description: IntroductionMonomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a very rare and aggressive type of gastrointestinal non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) with a poor prognosis.Case presentationA 59-year-old man presented with a three-days history of diffuse abdominal pain associated with distention and obstipation. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan showed small bowel obstruction (SBO) due to moderately thickened jejunal loop.

pmc-11484112.title: Comparison of the effectiveness of awake-prone positioning and high-flow nasal oxygen in patients with COVID-19-related acute respiratory failure between different waves
pmc-11484112.creator: Mariano Esperatti, Matías Olmos, Marina Busico, Adrian Gallardo, Alejandra Vitali, Jorgelina Quintana, Hiromi Kakisu, Bruno Leonel Ferreyro, Nora Angélica Fuentes, Argentine Collaborative Group on High Flow and Prone Positioning, Javier Osatnik, Santiago Nicolas Saavedra, Agustin Matarrese, Greta De
pmc-11484112.description: Objective:To compare the effectiveness of the awake-prone position on relevant clinical outcomes in patients with COVID-19-related acute respiratory failure requiring high-flow nasal oxygen between different waves in Argentina.Methods:This multicenter, prospective cohort study included adult patients with COVID-19-related acute respiratory failure requiring high-flow nasal oxygen. The main exposure position was the awake-prone position (≥ 6 hours/day) compared to the non-prone position.

pmc-12504170.title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals gut microbiota metabolite alterations and their correlation with serum biomarkers in gastric cancer patients from high-altitude regions
pmc-12504170.creator: Linghong Zhu, Zhaoxin Jin, Yanqing Ma, Xiao Feng, Caihong Ci, Yunsong Zhou, Qiaoling Gu, Yongmei Lan, Zilong Zhang
pmc-12504170.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to characterize gut microbiota-derived faecal metabolites and evaluate their associations with serum biochemical indices and tumor markers in gastric cancer patients residing in high-altitude regions, using untargeted metabolomics.MethodsStool samples from 30 newly diagnosed gastric cancer patients and 30 healthy controls from Qinghai Province were analyzed using LC–MS-based untargeted metabolomics.

pmc-12984062.title: Bifunctional glycolipids targeting TLR4·MD-2 and short pentraxins
pmc-12984062.creator: Daniele Zucchetta, Lena Nuschy, Simon Gumpelmair, Peter Steinberger, Iain Wilson, Holger Heine, Alla Zamyatina
pmc-12984062.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Innate immune detection of pathogen- and danger-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs/DAMPs) centres on pattern-recognition receptors, with the TLR4/MD-2 complex being uniquely sensitive to trace levels of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as well as infection-triggered endogenous ligands. While this axis rapidly induces protective cytokine production and upregulation of co-stimulatory molecules, its malfunction can cause pathological hyperinflammation culminating in systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), highlighting the importance of the development of TLR4 antagonists for the management of immunopathological disorders.

pmc-13268349.title: Effects of a health coaching program based on Cox’s interaction model in older adults with diabetes mellitus in Korea: a quasi-experimental study
pmc-13268349.creator: Hye Seung Kang
pmc-13268349.description: PurposeThis study aimed to evaluate the effects of a health coaching program based on Cox’s interaction model in adults aged 65 years or older with diabetes mellitus.MethodsA quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent control group and pretest–posttest measures was employed. Fifty-nine participants were assigned to either the experimental group (n = 30) or the control group (n = 29).

pmc-13455354.title: The cost of risk score and star rating growth: insights for future Medicare advantage innovation models
pmc-13455354.creator: Brett Lissenden, Allison Dorneo, John Robst, Peter F Lyu
pmc-13455354.description: IntroductionThe Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) may test a new Medicare Advantage (MA) innovation model for achieving broader Medicare efficiency. Informed by the MA value-based insurance design (VBID) model experience, we simulated minimum bid discounts and discussed strategies that would be needed to offset potential costs from plan risk score and star rating growth effects.

pmc-13677792.title: Prediction of bacteria-specific drug metabolism using a cross-attention-based model
pmc-13677792.creator: Jaehyeon Park, Si Eun Kim, Heeyoung Yang, Nam-Chul Cho, Hyunho Kim, Hyun Kil Shin
pmc-13677792.description: Drug metabolism by gut microorganisms is bacteria-specific and can have clinically significant consequences, including prodrug activation, drug inactivation, and the generation of toxic metabolites. However, existing computational approaches have primarily focused on community-level predictions or drug-to-microbe effects, without resolving the metabolic contributions of individual bacterial strains or the bidirectional nature of drug–bacteria interactions, despite advances in computational frameworks.
